messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert: kv-cache continuous-batching error rate spike + NCCL stalls detected on shard pool gpuprod-3. Paging increased, some hosts entering reclaim loops. Root TS: 2410001111

Ryan: I'm on it. Acknowledging page. @Priya can you join? Looks multi-GPU related.

Priya: I'm jumping in. Which jobs/nodes?

Maria: Metrics: kv-cache size per-shard jumped 6x in ~7m, continuous-batching queued tokens shot from 1.1k/s to 12k/s. Top noisy route: /generate/chat-stream. NCCL errors started ~2410001200 on nodes gpu-12,gpu-13 across AZ-a -> AZ-b.

Alex: Seeing repeated `ncclCommInitRank` timeouts and allreduce stalls in the runtime logs. Also observed uneven key partitioning — some shards have 4x the KV entries.

Jen: Customer impact: several mid-market customers reported 5xx and timeouts on hosted inference starting 2410001180. CS reported one support ticket escalated.

Luis: I've messaged affected customers that we're investigating, adding mitigation ETA 15m.

Priya: Hypothesis: a recent batching heuristic change allowed continuous batching to coalesce too aggressively, causing extremely large batches that expand KV cache usage and trigger cross-node NCCL handshakes with skewed shard sizes.

Ryan: Ok plan: 1) Disable continuous-batching at the routing layer (feature flag). 2) Roll back the batching heuristic. 3) Apply a quick KV-shard rebalancer to redistribute hot keys. 4) If needed, failover traffic to smaller model variant for affected customers.

Maria: Applying feature flag now: `POST /flags/continuous_batching:disable --env=prod` (canary cluster first).

DeployBot: Canary rollout started for flag `continuous_batching=false` on cluster canary-gpuprod-3 at 2410001255.

Priya: Observability note: enabling KV eviction logging to capture hotspot keys for the postmortem. Command:

```
kubectl exec -n runtime gw-logger -- /bin/sh -c "echo 'evict_log=1' > /etc/kv/flags && kill -HUP 1"
```

Alex: Patch ready for batching heuristic rollback, will push hotfix after canary confirms.

Ryan: Maria, any change in NCCL error rate after disabling continuous-batching on canary?

Maria: NCCL stalls dropped to near-zero on canary within 90s. Cache size on canary shards started decreasing. Good sign.

Priya: Okay push hotfix: revert batching heuristic (commit aa12bf) to prod with phased rollout. Alex, coordinate.

Alex: Deploying hotfix release aa12bf -> rolling to prod now. Watch for regressions.

DeployBot: Hotfix release aa12bf: canary->50%->100% completed. No new deploy errors reported.

Maria: Post-rollback metrics: global continuous-batch queue reduced to baseline within 6m. KV cache growth stabilized but several shards remain imbalanced.

Priya: Next step: run rebalancer to redistribute KV shards across GPUs to even out load. Running rebalancer in dry-run first.

Alex: Dry-run shows target ratio improvement from 4.2:1 -> 1.1:1 for entry counts. Proceeding with live rebalance with rate limit to avoid extra paging.

Ryan: Approved. Rebalance command (rate-limited):

```
python infra/tools/kv_rebalancer.py --cluster gpuprod-3 --max-migrations 50 --dry-run=false
```

Maria: Rebalance started at 2410001560. Migration events: ~42 keygroup moves over 18m. Memory pressure dropped incrementally.

Jen: SRE note: We saw two transient OOM warnings during migration on node gpu-16 but autoscaler prevented host termination. Need to capture logs and add to incident timeline.

Alex: Also applied a hotpatch to the shard assignment function to use consistent hashing with bounded imbalance (hotpatch id hp-2024-09-12). Deployed to service replicas.

Priya: Confirming: hp-2024-09-12 updated hashing, rebinds keys on migration to avoid skew on restarts.

Maria: After full rebalance and hashing hotpatch: NCCL error rate returned to baseline, per-shard KV sizes within 1.0-1.3x, API error rates back to <1% above norm.

Luis: Customer comms update: Notified impacted customers that mitigation completed; offering additional support slots. Affected customers acknowledged.

Jen: On-call handoff: Ryan -> Jen at 2410003000. Ryan, please include final checklist.

Ryan: Handoff summary: incident onset 2410001180. Root cause: overly aggressive continuous-batching heuristic causing massive batch coalescence -> KV cache blowups -> shard imbalance -> NCCL stalls. Mitigations performed: disabled continuous-batching flag, rolled back heuristic commit aa12bf, rebalanced KV shards, deployed hashing hotpatch hp-2024-09-12, scaled temporary rate limits on migrations. Current state: mitigated, services stable, monitoring for regressions. Follow-ups: postmortem, add eviction telemetry retention 14d, add automated shard-imbalance alerts, run chaos test for batching heuristic.

Jen: Got it. I'll own the postmortem. Assigning: Priya (root cause engineering), Alex (deployment + hotfix owner), Maria (metrics + timeline), Ryan (incident commander), Luis (customer comms). ETA draft postmortem in 48h.

Priya: Also recommend adding an emergency fallback policy: if NCCL stall rate > threshold, route new requests to single-GPU model variant until rebalance.

Alex: Filed follow-up issues:
- IMPROVE-789: Add bounded continuous-batch size and reject if exceeds token cap
- INFRA-342: Automated shard rebalancer runbook + safety checks
- OBS-221: Increase eviction log retention and add hotspot key dashboard

IncidentBot: Incident closed to active mitigation at 2410003600. Monitoring channel will run 24h watch. Postmortem assigned.

Ryan: TY everyone. Leaving notes in #postmortems once Jen publishes timeline.

Luis: I'll send a final customer summary after postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:

Jen: Handoff complete. Monitoring watch started. If any regression, page SRE oncall.
